title: Shannon collection shows wit and whimsy

notes: Use for object-level context; verify any specific Ultimate Machine construction details against a primary artifact or Shannon's own description before quoting them.

title: Claude Elwood Shannon, 1968
claim_or_use: Anchors Shannon at MIT in the late 1960s and provides an institutional collection trail for his later career and surviving artifacts.
notes: Context source rather than direct evidence for the Ultimate Machine.

title: Claude Shannon: Tinkerer, Prankster, and Father of Information Theory
claim_or_use: Provides sourced biographical chronology for Shannon's Gaylord childhood, radio and Erector-set tinkering, his sister Catherine's mathematics influence, and his University of Michigan double major.
notes: Secondary source; corroborate vivid childhood anecdotes with Soni/Goodman or archival material before using as scene detail.

title: Claude E. Shannon
claim_or_use: Confirms Shannon's birth and death dates and National Academy election year.
notes: Sparse institutional record; useful for chronology only.

title: Professor Emeritus Claude Shannon, founder of digital communications, dies at 84
claim_or_use: Confirms Shannon's work on Vannevar Bush's differential analyzer, the Boolean-algebra basis of his master's thesis, his MIT degrees, IAS fellowship, and move to Bell Labs.
notes: Reliable institutional chronology; avoid repeating the quoted 'master's thesis of the century' formulation unless attribution is retained.

title: A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits
claim_or_use: Primary evidence that Shannon represented relay and switching networks algebraically and identified the calculus with the symbolic calculus of propositions.
notes: Primary text; manuscript submitted March 1, 1938 and presented at the AIEE summer convention in June 1938.

title: Professor Emeritus Claude Shannon, founder of digital communications, dies at 84
claim_or_use: Confirms Shannon's part-time operation of Vannevar Bush's differential analyzer while at MIT.
notes: Use as chronology; seek Bush/MIT archival material before reconstructing the machine-room scene in detail.

title: Big achievements included room-size computers
claim_or_use: Places Bush's analog-computing work and Shannon's 1937-38 switching-circuit work within MIT's engineering chronology.
notes: Broad institutional timeline; not sufficient by itself for causal claims about what the differential analyzer taught Shannon.

title: A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits
claim_or_use: Primary evidence for the thesis's purpose, notation, network-synthesis method, and explicit analogy between switching algebra and symbolic logic.
notes: Quote sparingly from the original and distinguish the 1937 thesis from the 1938 published paper.

title: A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits (1938)
claim_or_use: Confirms the paper's canonical publication identity and later inclusion among foundational computer-science papers.
notes: Use for bibliographic cross-checking, not as evidence for historical reception in 1938.

title: Big achievements included room-size computers
claim_or_use: States that Shannon's master's thesis laid a theoretical foundation for modern computers in MIT's own historical timeline.
notes: Later retrospective characterization; keep separate from claims about contemporary reception.

title: Claude E. Shannon
claim_or_use: Confirms Shannon's membership in the IAS School of Mathematics from September 1940 through June 1941 and his 1940 MIT Ph.D.
notes: Use the dates as an institutional anchor; do not infer day-to-day contact with famous IAS figures without separate evidence.

title: Shannon, Claude E. -M-, 1940-41

notes: Primary archival trail for later close research; avoid reconstructing correspondence not yet inspected.

title: Claude Shannon Celebrated at IAS with Lecture by Sergio Verdú
claim_or_use: Confirms Shannon's 1940-41 IAS membership and the retrospective assessment that the 1948 paper created information theory.
notes: Useful for institutional context, not proof of particular conversations or friendships during 1940-41.

title: Professor Emeritus Claude Shannon, founder of digital communications, dies at 84
claim_or_use: Confirms that Shannon worked on secrecy systems at Bell Labs during World War II.
notes: Insufficient by itself for technical details of wartime cryptography; pair with Shannon's declassified secrecy paper for technical claims.

title: Research gap: Shannon-Turing meetings
claim_or_use: Flags the need for a primary or high-quality archival source establishing dates, setting, and substance of the 1943 Shannon-Turing meetings before narrative drafting.
notes: Do not write the tea/secrecy-clearance scene from popular retellings alone.

title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication
claim_or_use: Primary evidence for Shannon's general theory of communication, treatment of noise, statistical structure of messages, entropy, coding, and channel limits.
notes: Reprint notes original Bell System Technical Journal publication in vol. 27, July and October 1948.

title: Claude Shannon: The Father of the Information Age
claim_or_use: Provides a modern expert institutional account of the paper's historical impact across communication, computing, AI, probability, and statistics.
notes: Use as retrospective context; the 1948 paper remains the source for what Shannon himself claimed.

title: Claude E. Shannon
claim_or_use: Provides a concise institutional chronology locating the information-theory paper in July 1948 and describing its later significance.
notes: The page embeds a later New York Times account; distinguish that retrospective prose from IAS archival facts.

author_or_institution: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
title: Differential Analyzer Parts and Documentation
claim_or_use: Documents the first MIT differential analyzer as a room-sized mechanical analog computer completed around 1930 for solving differential equations, and describes surviving integrators, input-table carriages, and shaft-based function entry.
notes: Use for machine architecture and surviving components; do not infer Shannon-specific actions from the object record.

title: Mathematical Theory of the Differential Analyzer
claim_or_use: Primary evidence that Shannon later analyzed the differential analyzer mathematically, including what classes of functions and ordinary differential equations it could generate or solve.
notes: Supports sustained technical engagement with the analyzer and blocks the simplistic claim that Shannon merely rejected analog computing.

title: Vannevar Bush's differential analyzer
claim_or_use: Confirms the analyzer's large mechanical configuration, including six integrators and input/output tables that had to be connected for each new problem.
notes: Use for general machine operation and reconfiguration; avoid unsourced sensory reconstruction of Shannon at the controls.

title: The Essential Message: Claude Shannon and the Making of Information Theory
claim_or_use: Records Bush's suggestion that Shannon spend a summer at the Carnegie Institution genetics department at Cold Spring Harbor and that Shannon completed the theoretical-genetics doctorate in under a year.
notes: Secondary scholarly reconstruction based on papers, letters, and interviews; use for chronology while seeking the dissertation itself for technical claims.

title: Introduction to EECS II lecture materials
claim_or_use: Confirms Shannon's 1940 MIT mathematics Ph.D., titled An Algebra for Theoretical Genetics, and describes its purpose as analyzing dynamics of Mendelian populations.
notes: Institutional summary; do not inflate the thesis's later influence.

author_or_institution: Claude E. Shannon / Institute for Advanced Study Archives
title: Letter to the Office of the Dean, April 7, 1940
claim_or_use: Shannon states that he had received a National Research Fellowship in mathematics, hoped to take it at IAS, and proposed continuing his doctoral work applying higher algebra to theoretical genetics under Hermann Weyl.
notes: Primary evidence for Shannon's own intended research agenda; spelling artifacts in OCR should not be quoted without checking the scan.

title: Faculty and Staff Directory 1940-1941
claim_or_use: Provides a contemporaneous institutional record for the community in which Shannon held his 1940-41 membership.
notes: Use to establish institutional context, not personal interaction among members.

title: Communication Theory of Secrecy Systems
claim_or_use: Primary technical evidence for Shannon's wartime secrecy research: the published paper develops a mathematical theory of secrecy systems and states that its material first appeared in the confidential Bell Laboratories report A Mathematical Theory of Cryptography dated September 1, 1945.
notes: This declassified publication is strong evidence for the intellectual content and 1945 report lineage, but not for room-level scenes, particular wartime conversations, or Shannon's role in specific classified hardware projects.

title: Communication Theory of Secrecy Systems
claim_or_use: Bell Labs' archive preserves the paper and its stated scope: a general mathematical treatment of true secrecy systems rather than concealment or equipment-dependent privacy systems.
notes: Use as institutional provenance and for the paper's scope; Shannon's paper itself controls technical interpretation.

title: Research boundary: Turing encounter remains unverified
claim_or_use: Web research located repeated secondary claims that Shannon and Alan Turing met at Bell Labs in 1943, but no inspected primary archival record in this pass establishes the dates, tea-room setting, dialogue, or what either man disclosed.
notes: Keep Chapter 9 blocked for scene-level drafting. A later pass should seek Bell Labs correspondence, Turing travel records, or an archival oral-history transcript before narrating the encounter.
